problem: A hurricane is approaching the southern coast of Texas, and a rancher is planning to move some head of cattle 60 miles to higher ground to protect them from possible inland flooding that might occur. His animal transport truck holds 20 head of cattle. Traveling at 60 miles per hour, it took him 40 hours to transport all of his cattle to higher ground. How many head of cattle did the rancher have to move?

transcript.content: I'm confused about how to use the 40 hours and 60 mph to find the number of cattle. I know distance = rate × time, so 60 mph × 40 hours = 2400 miles, but that doesn't seem to relate to the 60-mile trip. Maybe I'm misreading the problem.
[ask_question] How many trips did the rancher make to transport all his cattle?
Distance is 60 miles, speed is 60 mph, so time per trip is 60 / 60 = 1 hour. Total time is 40 hours, so number of trips is 40. That makes sense. So he made 40 trips.
[correct_error] That's correct! You've figured out that the rancher made 40 trips. Now, if his truck can carry 20 head of cattle each trip, how many head of cattle did the rancher have to move?
40 trips times 20 head per trip = 800 head of cattle. So, he had to move 800 head.
